FINDING_ID: F001  
SEVERITY: 0.99  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.22  
DESCRIPTION: The Role Assignment area is not executable as given because several required support definitions are malformed or incomplete. `DynamicManagementConfig`, `CapabilityFingerprint`, and `ModelSpec` are presented with broken/incomplete bodies, and `RoleAssignment` calls methods/constructors on them (`get_alpha`, `as_array`, `as_normalised_array`, `ModelSpec(...)`) that are not actually implemented in the artifact. This blocks import, testing, and any downstream use of role assignment.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Provide complete, syntactically valid implementations for the Role Assignment support types in this area, or move non-area skeletons out of the executable module so the Role Assignment code can load independently.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002  
SEVERITY: 0.98  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.30  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment` uses dataclass fields (`field(...)`) and is instantiated via `cls(role_map=..., capability_scores=..., ...)`, but the class is missing `@dataclass`. Without a generated `__init__`, `assign()` will raise `TypeError` when it tries to construct `RoleAssignment`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `@dataclass` to `RoleAssignment` or implement an explicit `__init__` matching the constructor call sites.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `ModelSpec` is used with incompatible constructor shapes inside the same area. The validators call `ModelSpec("m1", fp)`, while `reassign()` reconstructs models with `ModelSpec(model_id=..., fingerprint=..., tau=..., L=..., c=..., L_std=...)`. At least one of these call patterns is wrong, so either validation or live-fingerprint reassignment will fail once `ModelSpec` is concretely defined.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define a single `ModelSpec` dataclass signature and use it consistently everywhere. For live updates, prefer `dataclasses.replace()` over hand-reconstructing the object.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` is nondeterministic on COL ties. `active_models` is a `Set[str]`, `remaining_ids` preserves that arbitrary set iteration order, `col_scores` is filled in that order, and `best_col_id = max(col_scores, key=lambda mid: col_scores[mid])` does not apply the documented lexicographic tie-breaker. Equal-score runs can therefore produce different COL assignments across executions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rank candidate `ModelSpec` objects directly with a key like `(adjusted_score, _tie_break_key(model), model_id)` and avoid using set iteration order as an implicit tiebreaker.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46  
DESCRIPTION: `get_ordering()` does not implement the same deterministic ordering rule used by assignment. It sorts only by raw score, so equal-score models are returned in insertion-order rather than by the plan’s documented lexicographic tiebreak. That makes the published capability ordering `≽_rho` weaker and potentially inconsistent with assignment behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Sort by `(score, _tie_break_key(model), model_id)` rather than score alone, using the actual model objects as the source of truth.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` decides whether a COL should exist using `len(self._models) >= 3`, which is the original pool size, not the current active pool size. If the run started with 3+ models but failures reduce it to 2 active models, `reassign()` still assigns a COL, contradicting the initial `assign()` logic where `K=2` yields only PM and PAR.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base the COL-existence decision on `len(active_models) >= 3` or an explicitly defined active-pool cardinality invariant.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` always inserts `self.pm_model_id` into `new_map`, even if that PM is absent from `active_models`. The returned role map can therefore contain an inactive or failed PM, which conflicts with the method’s `active_models` contract and can hide conditions that should trigger abort/escalation elsewhere.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate that the locked PM is active before reassignment. If it is not active, raise an error or hand control to failure handling rather than silently reintroducing it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: `capability_scores` are computed once in `assign()` and never refreshed in `reassign()`. After live fingerprint updates or failure-history penalties, `role_map` can change while `capability_scores` still reflect the initial state. This makes `get_ordering()` and any external consumer of `capability_scores` stale and inconsistent with actual assignment decisions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Recompute and store current scores during `reassign()`, or explicitly separate immutable initial scores from dynamic current scores in the API.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: There is no validation that `model_id` values are unique. Because `scores`, `role_map`, and `_failure_history` are all keyed by `model_id`, duplicate IDs will silently overwrite one another and cause models to disappear from assignment without any error.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject duplicate `model_id` values at the start of `assign()` and anywhere else a model list enters the system.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F010  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: The “PM locked for run duration (HARD)” constraint is not actually enforced at the object boundary. `pm_model_id` is publicly mutable, `role_map` is publicly mutable, and `reassign()` returns the same internal dict instance it stores. External code can therefore mutate the PM assignment or role map directly and violate C3 without passing through any guard.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make the PM identifier immutable, return defensive copies or immutable mappings, and encapsulate role changes behind validated methods only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F011  
SEVERITY: 0.36  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39  
DESCRIPTION: `round_idx` is accepted by `reassign()` but never used. The docstring says it matters “for failure history,” but the implementation ignores it entirely. That makes the API misleading and prevents the method from checking whether the recorded history actually corresponds to round `r-1` as claimed.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either use `round_idx` to index/validate failure-history state, or remove the parameter and update the contract to reflect the real behavior.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F012  
SEVERITY: 0.49  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43  
DESCRIPTION: The API does not fail fast on invalid model IDs. `record_failure()` silently creates history for unknown IDs, and `reassign()` silently skips unknown IDs in `active_models`. This masks caller bugs and can corrupt statistics or produce partial role maps without explanation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate all external model IDs against the known model pool and raise a clear exception on unknown IDs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F013  
SEVERITY: 0.31  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.20  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_homogeneous(k, config)` is not total over its own input domain. For `k <= 0`, it constructs an empty model list and calls `assign()`, which raises `ValueError` instead of returning `False` or a documented validator-specific error.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Guard `k >= 1` at the start of the validator and define the expected behavior for invalid `k` explicitly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F014  
SEVERITY: 0.29  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.28  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_homogeneous()` is too weak to validate the advertised reduction property. It checks only that there is exactly one PM and that PM scores are equal; it does not verify COL/PAR structure, deterministic winner selection, or reassignment behavior under homogeneous inputs. A broken implementation could still pass this validator.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Expand the validator to assert the full expected role pattern and deterministic tie resolution under homogeneous conditions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
